prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalyzed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling, a ligand-controlled method for forming aryl amines.

statement.case_for: Pd-catalyzed C-N coupling replaced harsh, narrow, substrate-limited routes to aryl amines with a general catalytic method. Its adoption is easy to verify: medicinal chemistry, process chemistry, materials and countless total syntheses use it routinely, and generations of ligands (Buchwald's biaryl phosphines, Hartwig's hindered alkyl phosphines and NHC systems) were designed from mechanistic understanding of oxidative addition, amine binding and C-N reductive elimination. The question I ask of any border-field nomination, what was new chemically, has a direct answer here: a bond that could not be formed reliably now is. Credit is also tractable. Buchwald and Hartwig independently built the general catalytic systems in the mid-1990s, and Kosugi's tin-amide work is a precedent rather than the general method. Thirty years of independent confirmation means no risk of an unstable interpretation.
statement.case_against: The 2010 prize for palladium-catalyzed cross-coupling (Heck, Negishi, Suzuki) means some colleagues will see this as a follow-on to a recognized area rather than a new principle, and a second synthesis-methodology prize in a short span after organocatalysis (2021) and click chemistry (2022) may look conservative against the modalities that are changing biology and medicine. Kosugi's precedent also leaves a small attribution blemish that the citation has to handle by wording the prize around the general catalytic method.

responses.point: Linke ranks Car-Parrinello first because the 1985 paper has exactly two authors, the credit is clean, and the method has four decades of independent use; he ranks C-N coupling fourth and flags the 2010 cross-coupling prize as a possible objection.
responses.response: I accept the attribution argument for B024 and the 40-year record, and it is a serious alternative. But the 2010 objection cuts less than he suggests. The 2010 prize recognised C-C bond formation with organometallic partners; C-N coupling needed different mechanistic solutions (amido complexes, beta-hydride elimination competing with reductive elimination, ligand design) and opened a different part of chemical space, the aryl amines that populate drugs. I also note that Car-Parrinello is a method for computing chemistry rather than a method for making molecules. I do not dispute its originality, but I would want to see what experimental chemistry it has changed, not only what it has made computable.

responses.point: Aqvist puts Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics first as a game-changer that connected electronic structure and atomic motion quantitatively to experiment, with clean two-person credit and overdue recognition.
responses.response: The clean credit is persuasive and I would not vote against B024 on science. My reservation is one of centre of gravity: its largest uptake is in condensed-phase physics and materials, and the claim of consequence for chemists everywhere is weaker than for a reaction used daily in laboratories. If the committee wants a theory or computation prize, B024 is the right one and I would support it as an alternative; I just do not see it displacing a method whose real-world adoption is so widely documented.

responses.point: Chabes ranks massively parallel sequencing first because reversible-terminator chemistry underlies genomics, and keeps the chemical-core pair (Balasubramanian, Klenerman) with Rothberg, Ju and Mayer contestable; he also ranks photoredox fourth, noting the 2021 organocatalysis prize as a reason for caution.
responses.response: I agree that the sequencing chemistry is real and the impact is beyond doubt, but the attribution problem is worse than he allows: Solexa, 454, Ion Torrent and Columbia terminator chemistries are different routes, and a three-person cap forces a choice between them that the record does not clearly make. On photoredox I share his concern about the 2021 prize and about priority among Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz, MacMillan and others; it is my second-ranked method candidate, but a cleaner prize can be written around C-N coupling.

responses.point: Aili ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles first as the delivery chemistry that made siRNA drugs and mRNA vaccines usable, favouring the Vancouver core, while admitting that apportionment with MIT and company teams is disputed.
responses.response: The pKa-tuned ionizable lipid is a real chemical design principle and the impact is demonstrated, so I take B064 seriously. My difficulty is that six credited names across academia and industry with contested priority cannot be fitted to three people without leaving out people the record also credits, and I am not able to judge the lipid and formulation priority myself. Given that, I would hold it as a strong candidate pending clearer attribution rather than make it the committee's first choice.

uncertainties: Whether a majority will accept that C-N coupling is conceptually distinct from the 2010 palladium cross-coupling prize rather than a follow-on.
Whether the committee prefers a prize aimed at a modality changing medicine (B046, B064, B012) over a core synthetic methodology prize, which is a values question rather than a factual one.
Whether Kosugi should be mentioned in the citation or text; I would leave the name out of the laureates but it is a judgement call.
Photoredox (B066) priority among Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz and others remains unresolved, as does the effect of MacMillan being a 2021 laureate.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: I have no known tie to Buchwald, Hartwig, Kosugi or the photoredox and degrader groups. My mentor was Masamune, who is not a candidate. I share Lund University with Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, but that creates no connection to the shortlisted candidates.
